recipes.name: Spaghetti Carbonara inspired by Master of None
ingredients: 7 oz all purpose flour (plus more for dusting)
1 cup grated parmesan (plus more for sprinkling)
all purpose flour (plus more for dusting)
grated rennet free parmesan (plus more for sprinkling)
instructions: For Carbonara #1:
For the Pasta

In a large bowl, whisk together both flours. Create a well in the center of the flours, and crack eggs inside. - 7 oz all purpose flour (plus more for dusting) - 7 oz semolina flour - 6 large eggs divided
Using a fork, beat the eggs together with the salt, gradually adding more and more flour, until a thick slurry is formed. - 1 tsp salt - 7 oz all purpose flour (plus more for dusting)

Begin kneading flour into the mixture with your hands, until a shaggy dough forms - turn out onto a floured surface and knead for 5 minutes, or until smooth and not tacky. - 7 oz all purpose flour (plus more for dusting)

Wrap in plastic wrap and let rest at room temperature for 30 minutes. NOTE: If you’re using a pasta extruder like in the video, you want a particularly dry dough - slightly rough to the touch (it will be kneaded further by the hopper). Add more flour as necessary. - 7 oz all purpose flour (plus more for dusting)
Using a pasta extruder, feed golfball-sized pieces of dough into the hopper with the stand mixer on high speed. - For the Pasta

Toss the pasta with flour before arranging into nests on a floured baking sheet, covering with plastic wrap, and refrigerating until ready to use (pasta freezes very well also). - 7 oz all purpose flour (plus more for dusting) - For the Pasta
Bring a pot of salted water to boil. - 1 tsp salt
For the Carbonara
In a large frying pan, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. - 1 tbsp vegetable oil
Cut the guanciale into lardons, and fry in the vegetable oil until crisp. - ½ pound guanciale (or pancetta/bacon) - 1 tbsp vegetable oil
As the guanciale finishes cooking, add the pasta to the boiling water and boil for 2-3 minutes, or until al dente. - For the Pasta
Add the minced garlic to the guanciale, and sauté until fragrant, about 30 seconds. - 2 ½ cloves garlic minced

Using tongs, remove the pasta from the pot, and place in the hot skillet (make sure you don’t drain the pasta too well, you want about 1/4 cup of pasta water to end up in the skillet). - For the Pasta
Remove the pan from the heat and toss the spaghetti with the guanciale. - For the Pasta - ½ pound guanciale (or pancetta/bacon)
Whisk together the remaining eggs and, stirring constantly, add to the hot pasta, and stir until thickened. - 6 large eggs divided - For the Carbonara

Toss with parmesan, season with pepper (and salt if necessary), and plate, topping with freshly grated parmesan. - 1 cup grated parmesan (plus more for sprinkling) - freshly ground pepper - For the Pasta
For Carbonara #2:

In a large bowl, whisk together both flours. Create a well in the center of the flours, and crack 4 of the eggs inside. - all purpose flour (plus more for dusting) - semolina flour - large eggs divided
Using a fork, beat the eggs together with the salt, gradually adding more and more flour, until a thick slurry is formed. - large eggs divided - salt - all purpose flour (plus more for dusting)

Begin kneading flour into the mixture with your hands, until a shaggy dough forms - turn out onto a floured surface and knead for 5 minutes, or until smooth and not tacky. - all purpose flour (plus more for dusting)

Wrap in plastic wrap and let rest at room temperature for 30 minutes. NOTE: If you’re using a pasta extruder like in the video, you want a particularly dry dough - slightly rough to the touch (it will be kneaded further by the hopper). Add more flour as necessary. - all purpose flour (plus more for dusting)
Using a pasta extruder, feed golfball-sized pieces of dough into the hopper with the stand mixer on high speed.

Toss the pasta with flour before arranging into nests on a floured baking sheet, covering with plastic wrap, and refrigerating until ready to use (pasta freezes very well also). - all purpose flour (plus more for dusting)
Bring a pot of salted water to the boil. In a large frying pan, heat the vegetable oil over medium flame. - salt - vegetable oil

Sauté the shiitake mushrooms until golden - as the mushrooms finish cooking, add the pasta to the boiling water and boil for 2-3 minutes, or until al dente. - shiitake mushrooms brushed clean, chopped
Add the minced garlic to the mushrooms, and sauté until fragrant, about 30 seconds. - garlic minced
Using tongs, remove the pasta from the pot, and place in the hot skillet (make sure you don’t drain the pasta too well, you want about 1/4 cup of pasta water to end up in the skillet).
Remove the pan from the heat and toss the spaghetti with the mushrooms.
Whisk together the two remaining eggs and, stirring constantly, add to the hot pasta, and stir until thickened. - large eggs divided

Toss with cheeses, season with pepper (and salt if necessary), and plate, topped with freshly grated parmesan. - grated rennet free parmesan (plus more for sprinkling) - ½ cup smoked provolone - freshly ground pepper - salt
